div.p: A better trip starts with knowing what the data can—and cannot—tell you.

Install the app on Splunk Enterprise with Python 3. Create a Queue-Times input in Settings → Data inputs. Enter park IDs or * for all parks. Select the queue_times index and a polling interval of at least 300 seconds.

Run one collector on an always-on host with outbound HTTPS access to queue-times.com. A sleeping laptop cannot collect missed snapshots. The public API supplies current data; history begins when you enable collection.

Our worldwide five-minute deployment used about 690 MiB/day—above the 500 MB/day trial limit. The Docker example keeps Disney World at five minutes and other parks at fifteen. Measure your own usage under Settings → Licensing.
Open Data Health, confirm recent successful polls, then check Live Explorer. Wait for completed days before treating patterns as useful planning evidence.

The app is tested locally on Splunk Enterprise 9.4.13. It is not Splunkbase-certified or AppInspect-certified. Use persistent volumes, protect administrator credentials, and do not expose the local development ports publicly.

div.span: Posted waits. Observed patterns. Your decisions.
